brief: A cover to hide the cables behind my TV and keep them tidy.

requirements.requirement: A cover to hide the cables behind a TV
requirements.evidence: Three full bases in a row (piece:-1,0,0, 0,0,0, 1,0,0) each closed on top with a cover (cover:...;full;top) set to cable type, plus capOpenFaces end caps, forming a continuous closed channel that hides cables inside.
A cable comb accessory in each cell (accessory:0#-1,0#1, 0#0,0#1, 0#1,0#1) to separate/order the bundle, and cable-coil prop staged on the centre cover.

requirements.requirement: Cables can enter and leave the cover
requirements.evidence: hex-port-gland cable plates at both ends (port:0#-1,0#2 and port:0#1,0#5) plus cable-type top covers for entry along the run.

requirements.requirement: Joints secured and open faces finished (house rules)
requirements.evidence: lockJoints added joint bolts between cells; capOpenFaces capped 7 open faces. check_build: ok, meshClash clear, one connected group.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell cable cover for behind a TV: three full hex bases in a row, each topped with a cable-type cover, a cable comb inside each cell to keep the bundle ordered, gland cable plates at both ends for entry/exit, end caps on all open faces, and joints bolted. A coiled cable prop on top shows it in use. Note: suitability for heat from the TV, specific TV/cable dimensions and wall-mounting are not checked by the configurator — it verifies fit only.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Hiding those TV cables in a tidy cover — first I'll survey the bench and the cable-ready covers on offer.
